headlines.title: Napa Valley wineries serve up new ‘experiences' amid sobering economic downturn
headlines.description: Tourism to Napa Valley historically brings in more than $2 billion each year, but fewer visitors and higher costs have winemakers across the region worried about an increasingly difficult financial landscape. “It’s not just the big guys that are getting hurt, it’s not just the little guys that getting hurt, it’s everybody in between,” said Christi Ficeli, owner of Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley. “This economy is hard for everybody, even the people that own wineries in Napa.” This economy is hard for everybody, even the people that own wineries in Napa Christi Ficeli, owner of Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley Ficeli, who runs the family-owned winery with her husband, Dave Ficeli, says visitation at the winery is down 40% from five years ago. “Cash is tight right now – the economy is tough on us,” she said. “Prices are increasing.” While Napa’s famed vintages are made locally, supplies often come from abroad and tariffs have resulted in higher prices. Wine barrels from France, glass bottles from China, and corks from Portugal have all increased in price, according to Ficeli, and rising gas prices have made those supplies even more expensive to transport. “Our costs have gone up 10% to 12% and our pricing has gone up 1% to 2%,” Ficeli said. “We’re absorbing a lot of that here.” Christi Ficeli has run Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley for the past 13 years with her husband Dave Ficeli. To offset higher costs, Ficeli’s winery is now focusing on more than just wine. To attract new customers and keep guests coming back, Goosecross has been hosting an array of events at its vineyard, including movie nights and comedy shows. “We’ve started doing more events because I think people want experience – they want things that are different,” she said. “We’re trying to bring some new and exciting things to the visitors that are here in Napa.” Ficeli is also investing in customer retention by recently expanding her staff from 12 to 13 employees, with the newest hire dedicated to keeping existing customers. Ellie Leigh was recently hired for the newly created customer-retention position. “Personal touch points, handwritten invitations, and notes has been really top of mind,” Leigh told Ficeli during a recent meeting at the winery. Ellie Leigh is the newest hire at Goosecross Cellars, where she is responsible for retaining customers and boosting wine subscriptions as the winery’s head of estate partnerships. I know it’s going to hurt to add another staff member, but if she can save a customer from leaving our program and keep them around for a little bit longer, it’s going to be worth every penny I’m spending on her. Winery owner Christi Ficeli explains why she hired a new employee to focus on customer retention “I know it’s going to hurt to add another staff member, but if she can save a customer from leaving our program and keep them around for a little bit longer, it’s going to be worth every penny I’m spending on her,” Ficeli told the Investigative Unit. “It’s so much more expensive to gain a new customer than to keep one.” For winery owners across Napa Valley, simply resting on the region’s laurels as a top-tier destination may no longer be enough to keep customers coming through the door. “It definitely has changed,” Ficeli said. “Mostly because there’s less people coming to Napa.” The region welcomed 3.8 million visitors last year, about 50,000 fewer than visited in 2018, according to Visit Napa Valley, Napa County’s tourism marketing organization. While Napa visitation has rebounded in recent years, it remains below its pre-pandemic peak. At the same time, fewer Americans are drinking wine. Only about 29% of adults in America drink wine compared to 34% three years ago, according to the Wine Market Council, a research firm that tracks consumer wine spending. Napa Valley tourism rates near pre-pandemic levels Adding to the challenge is the cost of traveling to wine country. The average hotel room in Napa Valley now costs about $420 a night – a 25% increase since before the pandemic, according to Visit Napa Valley. “We’ve done some estimates, it’s probably about $5,000 just to stay here for the weekend before you even walk through the door of a winery,” Ficeli said. “Hotel, flight, rental car, and food … all up.” Tasting prices have also climbed. The average tasting fee in Napa is now about $80, according to a recent wine industry report by Silicon Valley Bank. Food & Drink Jun 10 Napa County Apr 22, 2025 “We’re going through a really tough time,” said Tom Davies, who runs V. Sattui, a 50-year-old winery with more than 100 employees. “What’s at stake here is the sustainability of our wine industry.” Davies said the economy forced him to change pricing, too, but not in the way you might think. Two days a week, he dropped his tasting fee to zero to attract new business. We have to open our doors wider. Tom Davies, President and Managing Partner of V. Sattui Winery Tom Davies is president and managing partner of V. Sattui Winery in Napa Valley. “We have to open our doors wider,” Davies said. “I want to even be more accessible than we’ve ever been before.” Davies said the move to offer three complimentary pours has boosted wine sales. So much so, he’s now offering the free tasting menu three days a week. “We’re selling more wine than we were when we were charging every day,” he said. Davies remembers when all tastings in Napa were free. He said his idea to bring free tastings back is a nod to the past and an investment in the future – not only for his winery but for the entire Napa Valley. “The real payoff would be down the road when we can get the kind of visitation back to the vineyards that we had back 10 years ago,” he said. “I just want to make sure we can continue on.” Whether it’s larger wineries like his or smaller ones like Christi Ficeli’s down the road, the financial strain has been hard to swallow. I would say 2026 is one of the hardest years we’ve had so far outside of Covid. Christi Ficeli has run Goosecross Cellars for the past 13 years with her husband Winery owner Christi Ficeli takes Senior Investigative Reporter Bigad Shaban on a tour of her Napa Valley vineyard at Goosecross Cellars. “I would say 2026 is one of the hardest years we’ve had so far outside of Covid,” she said. “We’re working to cut costs everywhere we can.” Despite the financial squeeze, Ficeli remains hopeful. Like so many winery owners in Napa Valley, she’s holding on to a glass-half-full kind of optimism. “I love what I do,” she said. “When people come to Napa, they’re celebrating – 99.9% of the people who walk through our door are already happy and I get to make them that much happier by giving them an experience.” Contact The Investigative Unit submit tips | 1-888-996-TIPS | e-mail Bigad Follow @BigadShaban on social media Bigad Shaban This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: San Jose transportation worker killed while repairing streetlight
headlines.description: A San Jose Department of Transportation employee died Tuesday after being fatally injured while repairing a streetlight, according to city officials. San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, City Manager Jennifer Maguire, and Department of Transportation Director John Ristow issued a joint statement announcing the employee’s death while performing public service duties aimed at keeping drivers and pedestrians safe. “We are sad to share that a member of our City of San Jose family lost his life today while serving the public,” officials said in the statement. “We are deeply heartbroken about his passing and grateful for his public service.” City leaders did not immediately release the identity of the worker or specific details regarding the cause of the fatal injury. Following the incident, officials called on drivers to exercise caution near roadway work zones, urging the public to stay attentive, slow down, and provide adequate space for maintenance workers, construction crews, and emergency responders stopped in the street. “Our heartfelt condolences go out to his family, friends, and his department teammates during this incredibly difficult time,” the joint statement said.

headlines.title: Instagram head defends platform safety efforts in federal trial over youth addiction claims
headlines.description: State attorneys challenged the head of Instagram over whether the platform does enough to protect young users during a landmark federal trial accusing parent company Meta of designing intentionally addictive and dangerous features. Adam Mosseri testified in Oakland federal court Tuesday as part of a lawsuit brought by 29 states against Meta. Mosseri, who has led Instagram since 2018, denied claims that he knowingly concealed negative data from the public regarding the platform’s impact on young users. Mosseri is the first high-profile Meta executive to take the stand, telling the jury that he and his team prioritize the safety of younger users. His testimony followed statements from former Instagram employees who alleged the company ignored internal data showing youth encountered higher rates of bullying, hate speech, violent content, and suicide-related material than adults. “I think it’s really a bellwether, as many are describing it, to see how we move forward and how platforms can be held accountable and will be held accountable by legal courts and the court of public opinion,” said Nora Benavidez, senior counsel at Free Press. Former employees also testified that Meta knew fewer users would utilize Instagram’s “Take a Break” feature unless it was set as a default. Mosseri countered that focusing on a single feature overlooks Meta’s broader efforts to safeguard minors. Meta Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg is expected to testify later in the trial as the company defends itself against allegations that its social media platforms are knowingly addictive. “There’s no denying that these platforms are addictive, talk to any who says they’re begging themselves to be able to stop doomscrolling and you know that they’re addictive,” Benavidez said. Mosseri is expected to return to the stand to continue his testimony.

headlines.title: Dolly Parton remembered in Bay Area for music, advocacy and literacy impact
headlines.description: Dolly Parton’s legacy extends far beyond her decades of music, leaving a lasting impression in the Bay Area through both her artistic influence and her philanthropic work. In the children’s section of the main San Francisco Public Library, a life-sized cutout of the country music icon highlights her Imagination Library project. Over the past year, her partnership with the library system has delivered approximately 60,000 books nationwide to children enrolled in the program. “And even if they didn’t know her personally, she will have had a role in their life,” said Theresa Zighera, deputy director of the San Francisco Department of Early Childhood. “A really clear and meaningful role.” The effort ensures a lasting legacy even for youth unfamiliar with her extensive music catalog. “She’s left an impression on generations of people through her music, movies and television,” NBC Bay Area reporter Sergio Quintana said. “And even now Dolly Parton’s legacy will include leaving an impression on children, through books.” The San Francisco Public Library is one of more than 2,700 program partners across the country. Each local partner covers half the cost of mailing books directly to children, while the Dolly Parton Foundation or state grants fund the remaining half. “I know for Dolly, it was spurred by her own father who had struggles reading,” said Ruben Balderas, an early learning coordinator. “And she wanted to give kids, really, a leg up.” Music remained her primary gift to the world. During Pride Month, the San Francisco Gay Men’s Chorus paid tribute to Parton with a performance of her classic hit “9 to 5.” “I think the LGBTQ+ community connects with her so much because she woke up every day, decided how she wanted to live and did so courageously and publicly,” said Jacob Stensberg, artistic director of the San Francisco Gay Men’s Chorus. “And in doing so made us all believe that we could do that too.” Throughout her career, Parton performed numerous times across the Bay Area, including a 2005 appearance at the Hardly Strictly Bluegrass festival. She also appeared in local media interviews, including a December 2022 segment with NBC Bay Area’s Marcus Washington, where Washington asked if they could sing “We Wish You a Merry Christmas” together. “Aha, I don’t know if I know it well enough, are you going to take lead?” Parton joked in response. Following the announcement of her passing, her nephew Bryan Seaver shared a final message with her fans. “May God Bless Dolly Parton. And may God bless you all,” Seaver said. “She will always love you.”

headlines.title: San Jose police officer critical but stable after being shot by robbery suspect
headlines.description: A San Jose police officer was in critical but stable condition late Tuesday at Santa Clara Valley Medical Center after being shot by an armed robbery suspect earlier in the afternoon, according to police. The shooting occurred in the area of Lick Avenue and Goodyear Street. An advisor to San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan said the mayor planned to visit the officer at the hospital, and his office later indicated that the visit took place. While law enforcement agencies have not released an official statement regarding the condition of any officers or suspects involved, sources told NBC Bay Area that an officer was down and a suspect was neutralized. A source indicated the officer is potentially doing better and possibly in stable condition, though officials have not confirmed that status. Additionally, a possible second person involved in the incident was taken to the hospital, though their condition remains unknown. A heavy police presence was reported nearby at Almaden Avenue and Floyd Street, where a local resident reported seeing officers from the San Jose Police Department and deputies from the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office with guns drawn, alongside a potential response from university police. Witnesses reported seeing an individual down on the ground and expressed concern that a subject may have barricaded themselves, though police have not verified those accounts. A local family in the area told NBC Bay Area that a suspect entered their home and held family members hostage before escaping. Authorities have not confirmed that account or stated whether that incident is connected to the shooting. By late Tuesday evening, much of the scene outside Santa Clara Valley Medical Center—where caution tape previously blocked the entrance alongside a heavy law enforcement presence—had dispersed and quieted down. Department public information officers noted that the investigation remains active and ongoing, with additional official details regarding what led up to the gunfire and the condition of the officer expected to be released as they become available.
headlines.source: Pete Suratos, Ali Reid and Erik Gabaldon

headlines.title: Results revealed from San Jose poll to rename downtown plaza
headlines.description: Results from a public poll to rename San Jose’s downtown plaza were revealed Tuesday. San Jose is looking to rename the plaza, which for 33 years carried the name of late labor leader Cesar Chavez, after his name was removed in March following allegations of sexual assault and misconduct. The top two choices from the poll are Plaza de San Jose, which led with 40% of the vote, and Farmworkers Plaza. About 10,000 San Jose residents participated in the multiple-choice poll to rename the plaza. A committee with San Jose Parks, Recreation and Neighborhood Services will now recommend the top choice to the parks and recreation commission, who will then vote on Sept. 2 whether to advance it to the city council for consideration. San Jose’s city council is expected to make a final decision on the plaza’s new name in late October. headlines.title: Senior residents in Oakland building raise safety, maintenance concerns
headlines.description: Seniors living in a low-income housing building in downtown Oakland say their safety and maintenance concerns are being ignored. With the help of translators and tenant advocates, the mostly Cantonese-speaking community held a rally Tuesday to complain about recent break-ins, hot water problems and a lack of concern by management at Southlake Tower. “I really hope that the building management respects us tenants as elders and that they would properly listen to our comments and our demands and to be able to work it out with the landlord to resolve our issues,” resident Fei Peng said through a translator. A week ago, an elderly couple woke up to find someone prying into their fifth floor apartment. They said the person ran away without harming anyone. “Every night now since the break-in, I put a chair up against my door so if somebody breaks in, I can hear it and maybe use my pepper spray or something,” resident Francine Broadnax said. Broadnax voiced other concerns, saying sometimes there’s no hot water or it suddenly goes from cold to scalding. “Can you imagine being in the shower and then all of a sudden the water gets scalding hot?” she said. “It’s crazy-making.” Residents also said management locks the first floor community center and bathroom at 5 p.m. and on weekends. Residents said Christian Church Homes management, which operates the building, hadn’t responded to their ongoing complaints – until Tuesday. NBC Bay Area witnessed staff sprucing up the downstairs, and several managers showed up to talk to reporters. “We will hear concerns,” said Avni Desai with Christian Church Homes. “We will continue to engage and make sure we do better and that this is a place they’re proud to call home.” Managers said they fixed the water issue Tuesday and will continue to address security concerns.

headlines.title: San Jose to remove more dead or dying trees
headlines.description: More dead or dying trees in San Jose will soon be cut down. Last week, the city started to remove 32 trees in the Circle of Palms downtown because they were diseased and at risk of falling. Now, the city plans to tear out nearly three dozen more trees on Zanker Road. The city tagged 35 trees along the Zanker Road meridian and said the scheduled removal over the coming weeks is not up for debate. “Many of the trees are already either completely dead or on their way there – they’re dying,” said Colin Heyne with the city’s Department of Transportation. “That’s why they’re posted pink. They don’t have a protest period like a tree removal typically would. There’s no going back for these trees. We will be removing them.” The struggling trees include loquats, purple leaf plums and European olive trees – greenery that simply does not do well in the current location. “They’re not suitable for the growing conditions right there in the median of a busy street or the drought conditions that we face here in San Jose,” Heyne said. The city plans to replace the uprooted trees with 100 new ones that are better suited to the area. headlines.title: Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri takes stand in landmark Meta trial over child safety
headlines.description: This live blog has ended and is no longer being updated. A pivotal trial for Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, is underway in Oakland. The high-profile federal trial puts the state of California against Meta, as a judge and jury weigh whether social media platforms are intentionally addictive and harmful to children. Adam Mosseri, Instagram’s chief executive, is expected to testify Tuesday. NBC Bay Area’s Scott Budman is at the courthouse and providing live updates. View the latest below. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

headlines.title: 49ers owner Jed York texted woman he believed was prostitute before arrest
headlines.description: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday. The report from the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force had more than two pages redacted but provided more details about what led to York’s arrest and ultimately to him pleading no contest Monday to two misdemeanors. York initially responded to an advertisement placed by police on a known prostitution website on Saturday, according to the report, sending two messages that went unanswered and saying his name was “Joe” and that he wanted to visit the woman. York texted again Sunday morning and said he wanted to see the woman. He said he was staying nearby and asked for her address. He asked how much the woman charged and was told it was $160 for “full service sexual activity,” the report said. York took a rental car to a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio, where he was given a fictitious lot number. He texted when he arrived at the mobile home park. He was then directed back to the main road, where he was stopped by marked police units. Police found York had $160 that was seized and they sent a text to his phone to determine it was the same one used to arrange the meeting. He was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest Monday to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the ad. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. The $160 that was seized from him was given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course. York has been in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown, for most of the summer. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records. The NFL issued a statement saying the league is aware of the arrest and will review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the policy. The team said that the “legal matter” had been resolved and that it would have no additional comment. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that he has talked to York the past two days and doesn’t believe the arrest will have any impact on the team. “Obviously, it’s a very tough situation,” Shanahan said. “The views for the organization going forward are the same as usual. There won’t be any difference in that. But I know it’s extremely fresh. I think it’s a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got lot of respect for Danielle. The family does mean a lot to me. With it being this personal, I’m trying as hard as I can to keep it that way.” Shanahan said he doesn’t expect any change in York’s involvement with the team, saying he has always allowed Shanahan and general manager John Lynch to make the football decisions. Shanahan said he doesn’t feel the need to address the situation with his players. Star linebacker Fred Warner said the players were aware of it but that he didn’t believe it would be a distraction. “We all have social media, so we see things,” he said. “But at the same time, I got a lot of love, a lot respect for Jed, and don’t feel the need to comment on the situation. I think the team is kind of the same way. It really wasn’t a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but at the time, we were so hyper-focused in this building of trying to prepare for Week 1. A lot of guys are on the bubble trying to make the team. So we’re just trying to get better as a football team and that’s a personal situation, and letting it stay personal with him.”

headlines.title: Woman, dog fatally struck by driver in Novato
headlines.description: A 59-year-old woman and her dog died Monday night after being struck by a driver while crossing a street in Novato, police said. Novato police responded around 9 p.m. to the collision near Novato Boulevard and St. Paul Circle. Police said the woman was crossing the road with her dog when she was struck by an eastbound sedan driven by an 18-year-old man. The woman was rushed to a hospital, where she later died from her injuries. Her dog also passed away. The driver remained at the scene and is cooperating with investigators. Police said impairment does not appear to have been a factor in the collision. The Novato Police Department’s Traffic Investigation Team and crime scene investigators are handling the collision investigation. The Marin County Sheriff’s Office Coroner Division is investigating the woman’s death and has not yet released her identity. Anyone with information about the collision can contact Novato Police Traffic Sgt. Trevor Hall at 415-897-4361.

headlines.title: Video shows Muni operator appearing to be dozing off seconds before SF train crash
headlines.description: Newly released video footage obtained through a public records request shows a San Francisco Municipal Railway operator appearing to fall asleep at the controls seconds before crashing into another Muni train, an incident transit officials attribute to operator fatigue. The collision occurred around 8:30 a.m. on July 31 near 47th Avenue and Wawona Street in the Outer Parkside neighborhood. Onboard camera footage shows the operator nodding off while the train moves down the track. He wakes up moments later, looks ahead, realizes the train in front of him is too close, and braces for impact. The crash shattered the train’s front windshield. Two passengers were on board at the time, and no injuries were reported. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency said its initial investigation ruled out equipment failure or infrastructure problems, pointing instead to operator fatigue as the cause. “It definitely concerns me as a rider,” said Muni passenger Peter Dignadice. “When drivers have to run these tight shifts… I can see them getting tired and this being an issue.” The incident marks the second time in less than a year that a Muni operator has been captured on camera apparently dozing off at the controls. Last September, separate footage showed another operator appearing to sleep while driving through the Sunset Tunnel. “I really hope the bus drivers are taking care of themselves and but also that SFMTA is taking care of their employees,” said San Francisco resident Jade Tu. In response to fatigue concerns, the SFMTA stated that it “has increased random video reviews to ensure safe vehicle operation and allocated additional rest time on all operator shifts to proactively address fatigue.” District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong called the crash “unacceptable to happen in our city” while attempting to reassure riders about the transit system’s overall safety. “I understand this is concerning for people in the neighborhood… but at the same time this was a limited incident,” Wong said, noting he wants to determine whether the crash represents an isolated event or a systematic issue. The operator involved in the collision has been placed on non-driving status. The SFMTA is continuing its investigation in coordination with the California Public Utilities Commission.
